g1-address-implement.title: G1 address value object: implement
g1-address-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. TASK: in src/physics/fingerprint/address.py add a frozen dataclass SlotAddress(driver, era, vocabulary_version, channel, what_measure) carrying EXACTLY the validation CellAddress already enforces -- each field a non-empty str, none containing CELL_KEY_DELIMITER, what_measure in _KNOWN_WHAT_MEASURES -- with ValueError messages that name the offending field, its expectation and its actual value (project rule). Re-express CellAddress as slot + class_id so the validation rules exist in exactly ONE place: either CellAddress composes a SlotAddress, or both delegate to one module-private validator. Add SlotAddress.for_vocabulary(driver, vocabulary, channel, what_measure) deriving era from vocabulary.rules_era, and a slot->cell accessor (e.g. SlotAddress.cell(class_id) -> CellAddress). *** CRITIC FINDING F1 -- THE LANDMINE, READ THIS TWICE *** CellAddress.cell_key MUST produce a byte-identical string to today's for every input: it is a STORED PRIMARY KEY, so a changed join order silently orphans every row in every existing driver_fingerprint.db with no test failure. The current order is _CELL_KEY_FIELD_NAMES = (driver, era, vocabulary_version, class_id, channel, what_measure) -- note that class_id is at POSITION 4, NOT LAST. The natural 'slot + class_id' composition puts class_id LAST and is therefore WRONG. Preserve the existing order explicitly. The characterization test must assert a HARD-CODED expected cell_key string (e.g. 'VER|drs1-mguk1-mguh1|severity:v1|severity:v1:c0|utilization|deficit'), NOT a value recomputed from _CELL_KEY_FIELD_NAMES -- a test that recomputes from the same constant passes happily after a reorder and proves nothing. Add SlotAddress unit tests to tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_address.py alongside the existing CellAddress ones. THIS GATE IS PURELY ADDITIVE: do not touch store.py, fit.py, pilot/pipeline.py, any script, or any call site. The suite must be green at this gate boundary.

g2-store-implement.title: G2 store retype + call-site migration: implement
g2-store-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. TASK, ATOMIC IN ONE GATE (splitting it guarantees a red suite between gates): retype DriverFingerprintStore.write_fingerprint, .get_fingerprint and .row_count to take a SlotAddress in place of the five loose primitives (driver, era, vocabulary_version, channel, what_measure), keeping the separate vocabulary argument and, for write, observations. HARD CUTOVER -- no primitives-accepting overload, no deprecation shim (engine-config rules_root: one clear execution path; an overload would preserve the very unvalidated path this gate exists to close). Migrate EVERY call site, enumerated: src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:356; src/physics/pilot/pipeline.py:257 and :325; scripts/fingerprint_bounded_validation.py:124; scripts/join_bounded_validation_667.py:173; tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_store.py (27 occurrences), test_fit.py (10), test_bounded_validation.py (7). All are POSITIONAL, so a missed site is a TypeError at collect time. Inside write_fingerprint, build each row's CellAddress from the slot via the g1 accessor rather than re-constructing it field-by-field. ADD the H1 acceptance test -- and note CRITIC FINDING F2 on WHERE the refusal lives: once the signature takes a SlotAddress, a malformed address can no longer REACH the store; it fails at SlotAddress CONSTRUCTION. Do NOT add a redundant re-validation inside get_fingerprint/row_count -- that would re-create the two-places-to-forget problem this whole gate exists to remove. The acceptance test therefore asserts BOTH: (a) SlotAddress construction raises ValueError naming the field for driver='', driver=None, and a driver containing CELL_KEY_DELIMITER; and (b) the store method is unreachable with a bad address by type -- there is no primitives path left to smuggle one in. Contrast with today, where those same inputs make get_fingerprint silently return k synthesized 'unresolved' cells. PROTECTED, must remain observably identical: the four store invariants (non-NULL cell_key; exactly k cells always, unresolved never missing; all four loud-refusal arms incl. EraVocabularyMismatchError and ReservedWhatMeasureError; no fit-on-read). _check_era_vocabulary_argument_consistency stays live and guard-tested even though SlotAddress.for_vocabulary cannot produce a mismatch -- the explicit constructor still can, and the refusal must not be deleted. A read for a legitimately ABSENT driver must still return k unresolved cells; do not conflate 'malformed' with 'missing'.

g3-scripts-implement.title: G3 script path guard + artifact anchoring + narrow ignore: implement
g3-scripts-implement.imperative: Fill templates/IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md and dispatch constellation-implementer. THREE bounded changes. (H2) In scripts/fingerprint_class_coverage_675.py add the house worktree-first guard verbatim in the form used at scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:71-75 -- _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]; if str(_REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path: sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT)) -- placed AFTER the stdlib imports and BEFORE the numpy/scipy/src imports at lines 95-100, with `import sys` added. This works because the editable install APPENDS its finder to sys.meta_path (verified in site-packages/__editable___f1brainz_0_2_0_finder.py), so sys.path is consulted first. (H3) Re-anchor the two path constants that are currently bare relative Paths -- DEFAULT_SLICE_DB (:122) and VERDICT_PATH (:123) -- on _REPO_ROOT, and add an --out argument beside the existing --slice-db so the verdict destination is overridable; today a bare run from any cwd mkdir -p's and writes a stale pre-archive .agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/ tree (that work area was archived on 2026-07-26). (H3b) Add to .gitignore a NARROW rule covering only the live pre-archive artifact path .agent-work/666-driver-fingerprint/artifacts/. CRITIC FINDING F3 -- H3a AND H3b ARE COUPLED, SHIP BOTH OR NEITHER: before re-anchoring, a bare run scattered its output relative to whatever cwd it ran from (sometimes outside the repo entirely); AFTER re-anchoring it writes under _REPO_ROOT every time, which GUARANTEES the stray lands inside the tracked tree. So the ignore rule is not belt-and-braces here, it is REQUIRED BY the anchoring change, and landing the anchoring without the ignore makes H3 strictly worse than doing nothing. DO NOT add a blanket .agent-work/**/*.json rule (tc2 as originally worded): .agent-work/ is a TRACKED directory here and the archived JSONs under .agent-work/archive/**/artifacts/ are committed durable evidence by the repo's own archive-then-commit convention -- a blanket rule would silently un-track the evidence trail across 664/666/667/669/670. A grep-for-the-guard-line test is a proxy and is not accepted.
